# Orihon

Orihon is a TypeScript browser mapping library.

For AI-generated maps prefer `orihon/ai`. It accepts versioned, JSON-only scenes and
machine-readable commands. For ordinary application code prefer `orihon/easy`.

Imports:

    import { createMap } from "orihon/easy";
    import { createAISession, applyScene } from "orihon/ai";
    import "orihon/orihon.css";

Coordinate rules:
- Orihon AI coordinates are objects: `{ "lat": 55.75, "lng": 37.61 }`.
- Coordinate arrays are not accepted by the AI API.
- GeoJSON remains standard longitude-first: `[37.61, 55.75]`.

Scene rules:
- Use `version: 1`.
- Every layer has a stable, unique `id`.
- Layer types are `marker`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `geojson`, and `raster`.
- Popup and tooltip content is plain text: `{ "text": "Moscow" }`.
- Functions, DOM nodes, class instances, `undefined`, and non-finite numbers are rejected.

Server/agent rules:
- `createAICommandEngine()` is headless and owns canonical revisioned JSON state.
- Prefer `createAIIntentTool(createAIAgentRuntime(engine))` for semantic goals; it plans through
  registered ObjectManager and Route Model capabilities and commits atomically.
- `create_visit_route` routes are reactive by default: collection changes trigger engine-side
  replanning without another model call.
- `createAIHTTPHandler(engine)` exposes snapshot, command, and SSE endpoints.
- Semantic HTTP endpoints expose capabilities, compact context, intent preview, and intent commit.
- `createAIMapProjection(map)` applies server events in the browser.
- Live domain entities use `objects.*` commands and stable GeoJSON feature IDs.
- Object deltas flow through `FeatureSource` into `ObjectManager`.
- Named point maps can use `points.replace` with declarative popups, circular `visual.image`, hover-first `visual.label`, and `viewport.mode:"fit"`.
- `route.plan` orders an existing point collection and projects its RouteResult through RoutingLayer.
- `createAIEngineTool(engine, { profile })` supports `full`, `scene`, `objects`, `points`, `routes`, and `readonly` schemas.
- Engine tool results are compact by default; HTTP and SSE retain complete revisioned events.
